result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_all_loops()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count total number of self-loop edges in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4728-L4776){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_all_loops() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A self-loop is an edge where the source and target are the same node. This counts all self-loop edges in the entire graph, regardless of which nodes they belong to. Use `count_loops()` to get per-node counts. Self-loops are common in state machines, reflexive relationships, and chemical reaction networks. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of edges where source equals target. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two of these three edges connect a node to itself, so `count_all_loops()` reports `2`: ::: {#7410e4ea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("A", "A") # self-loop .add_edge("B", "B") # self-loop ) graph.count_all_loops() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Self-loops stack: adding two self-loops on the same node counts both: ::: {#c2b1e6fe .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_edge("A", "A") graph.add_edge("A", "A") graph.count_all_loops() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
